learning_outcomes.text: Students can apply basic calculation methods for flow and work processes in turbomachinery to assess their energetic behavior and typical design features.
Students can perform simple balances based on conservation laws for mass, momentum, and energy to computationally determine thermodynamic and mechanical quantities in rotating machines.

Students can model more complex components with modern Finite Element programs (e.g., ABAQUS/CAE) by selecting suitable element types, boundary conditions, and load cases to numerically analyze realistic structural behavior.
Students can assess the quality of Finite Element meshes and adjust basic simulation parameters to improve the significance of their models.
Students can numerically investigate linear and nonlinear structural problems as well as basic stability and dynamics phenomena to evaluate technical correlations in practical applications.

syllabus_topics: Complementary meshing techniques and evaluation of mesh quality
Material models for describing anisotropic and plastic material behavior
Determination of material properties and fitting a flow curve
Heat transfer (steady and unsteady) and thermomechanical calculations
Linear dynamics: Modal analysis and harmonic analysis (influence of damping)
Nonlinear FEM: Remeshing, time step control, process simulation and damage models, strain and stress components
Conservation equations and balancing in turbomachinery
Operating behavior of various types of turbomachinery

assessment_methods.method: Successful participation in all laboratory experiments (prerequisite for exam admission)

assessment_rules: The module exam is a 120-minute written exam with aids. A prerequisite for admission to the exam is successful participation in all laboratory experiments. The exam consists of two partial exams, whose individual grades are weighted by SWS to determine the overall grade.
